published_prior_art.cite: ShyamalZhangUhler2025 proves a near-optimal limited-supply result only for k=1; SchwabeWong1999 supplies product-design machinery but not this shared-supply all-order A-optimality theorem.
Tropp2012 supplies matrix Chernoff and HsuKakadeZhang2014 supplies general random-design analysis; neither states this Boolean product-design calibration and zero-fallback risk decomposition.
ShyamalZhangUhler2025 gives passive near-optimal risk control, while the proposed result specializes the exact all-order optimum and leverage-calibrated threshold.
DerezinskiWarmuth2017 obtains exact inverse-Gram identities for dependent volume sampling, not the stated independent product-dosage minimax saddle problem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Proceedings record and abstract; companion public PDF search text, Section 5.1 and Theorem 5.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper uses independent product-Bernoulli dosage; its limited-supply closed-form theorem is for the additive k=1 model, while non-additive models are treated by numerical optimization.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics 51(4), 1999
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article is a product-design A-optimality paper and explicitly reports formulas beyond additive models; no contrary theorem claim was located.
The paper supplies tail inequalities for sums of independent random self-adjoint matrices, the relevant concentration engine.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Published article record; corroborating COLT version, Introduction and Section 3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work analyzes OLS and ridge under random design and separates covariance-estimation and model-error effects; it does not provide the proposed product-Fourier specialization.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Pages 1-2, abstract and equations for volume sampling
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under dependent volume sampling, the paper gives unbiased pseudoinverse/least-squares estimates and exact inverse-Gram expectation formulas.
The paper studies D-optimality on symmetrically restricted two-level design regions with first-order interactions, a different assignment class and criterion.
The paper derives allocation results for complete and block randomized 2^K factorial experiments under A-, D-, and E-optimality, not independent coordinate dosage.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Article abstract and reported interaction findings
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Compressed Perturb-seq is a plausible high-multiplicity screening consumer, but it does not establish the proposal's independent-delivery or homoskedastic Fourier model.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Solve the finite-n minimax frontier for a nontrivial small k regime, including an explicit nonuniform winning dosage region; this would turn the retained OEQ into a second independent design contribution.
Add an exact comparison of the A-optimal uniform design with PFED's minimum-eigenvalue near-optimal criterion, identifying parameter regimes where the two criteria choose provably different dosages.
State a worked numerical symbolic corollary for k=2 or k=3 that converts the leverage and rank-obstruction formulas into an explicit sample-size rule.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with thm:uniform-optimum as the field-tier kernel; retain the finite-risk frontier as a clearly separated open extension.
